title: The Wild Veil Again
premise: Dominic Reyes, a mercenary bound by oath to the Silent God, has spent his life in the valley where magic cannot follow — until his name and today's date surface in a century-old book of prophecies. Pulled beyond the valley's edge with the exiled scholar Wren Halloway, he discovers the kingdom's king is slowly being consumed by an ancient entity wearing his crown as a vessel. To save both king and realm, Dominic must break his oath to the Silent God, whose silence is revealed to be not absence but imprisonment — the entity devoured it long ago. In the end, Dominic sacrifices his inherited bond to the god to shatter the crown-entity, freeing the king, restoring magic's balance, and choosing loyalty to people over truth to powers that never answered.
about_author: Sebastian Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and curse-formulae before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken promises, haunted institutions, and the people stubborn enough to keep faith anyway.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't His
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the oath-house library, Wren Halloway shows him a prophecy book naming him and tonight's date. Dominic dismisses it as forgery until the valley's magic-dead boundary shudders and pulls them both through. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as the safe world proves porous.

chapters.title: Beyond the Veil
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pair lands in the capital on coronation eve; magic floods back into Dominic's senses painfully. Wren deciphers more prophecy: 'the crowned thing shall finish its meal.' They witness the king at a window, eyes flickering wrong. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The King Who Blinks Twice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Posing as pilgrim guards, they enter the palace and meet Prince Aldric, who privately admits his father speaks in two voices. A court mage tests Dominic and finds the mark of the Silent God on him — dangerous, since the god was declared dead. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming under surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Oath Bought
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback interwoven: how Dominic's family inherited their oath generations ago in exchange for the valley's protection. Present-day Wren finds records showing every oath-bearer died within sight of the throne. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a trap dressed as devotion.

chapters.title: The Feast of Two Voices
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the coronation feast, the entity wearing the king publicly senses Dominic's god-mark and offers him power to abandon his silent master. Dominic refuses; assassins strike; Aldric helps them flee into the undercity. Emotional beat: temptation met and survived, but now hunted.

chapters.title: Where Gods Go Quiet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the catacombs beneath the old temple, they find the Silent God's prison-shrine: the entity didn't kill it, it swallowed its voice. Wren learns unbinding requires an oath-bearer willing to surrender the bond entirely. Emotional beat: grief for a god who suffered all along.

chapters.title: Aldric's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aldric proposes seizing the crown to end the possession by force, asking Dominic to swear fealty to him instead of the god. Dominic nearly accepts — a new master for an old chain — before realizing the cycle would merely repeat. Emotional beat: the seduction of swapping one corruption for another.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured by the court mage, Wren is shown the truth: the first king forged the crown-entity deliberately to make rule immortal, and every heir since has been its meal. Wren escapes with the binding rite but loses the prophecy book. Emotional beat: fury at power that feeds on inheritance itself.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Climax in the throne room during the entity's full ascension. Dominic begins the rite, offering his oath-bond as the key; the Silent God's voice returns long enough to release him willingly. He shatters the crown-entity, freeing the king at the cost of his lifelong identity. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation, not loss.

chapters.title: The Valley, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later: the king recovers, Aldric reforms the succession, and magic now flows gently where the valley stood sealed. Dominic, oathless and free, chooses to stay near Wren rather than return to what he was. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — loyalty finally given freely, not inherited.
